sentences.text:

Heard Sri Abdus Saleem, learned counsel for the petitioner; Sri Niranjan, learned counsel appearing for respondents 1 and 4 and Sri Ajay, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home appearing for respondents 2 and 3.
2.
The case of the petitioner, in brief, is that the petitioner made an application dated 11.03.2022 (Ex.P2) for re-issuance of passport, however, the same was not issued.

As seen from the status report dated 27.01.2025 (Ex.P1), the passport was not issued on the ground of the police verification report is not clear and the application is under review at the Regional Passport Office.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner was initially issued a passport on 06.09.2012 for ten years and the same expired on 05.09.2022.
Even before the expiry period, the petitioner made an application on 11.03.2022.
However, the same was not issued.

He would submit that the case in Crime No.406 of 2016 of IV Town Police Station, Vishakaptnam was registered against the petitioner and others for the offences under Sections 420, 498A r/w 34 IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
Later police filed a charge sheet on the file of I Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Vishakaptnam.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel would also submit that the charges are framed by the learned Magistrate and C.C.No.334 of 2018 is coming up for trial (examination of witnesses).
4.

Learned counsel appearing for the respondents would submit that since the charges are framed and the learned Magistrate has taken cognizance of the offences and framed charges, the petitioner has to approach the learned Magistrate by making a proper application.
5. Thus, as seen from the material, there is no dispute about the issuance of a passport to the petitioner on 06.09.2012 for ten years (Ex.P4).
It is also an undisputed fact that the petitioner made an application for re-issuance of passport on 11.03.2022 and the same has not been issued so far.

As per the status report dated 27.01.2025 (Ex.P1), it was mentioned that since the police verification report is not clear and the application made by the petitioner is under review at Regional Passport Office .

6. The Division Bench of this Court in W.A.No.383 of 2024 considered Section 6(2)(f) of Passports Act, 1967 and the judicial proceedings pending against the individual and cognizance for the offences by the Magistrate.
The writ appeal was disposed of directing the petitioner therein to approach the jurisdictional Magistrate to seek appropriate orders for re-issuance of passport.

The Division Bench of this Court in W.A.No.383 of 2024 observed as follows:
"Therefore, we would have no hesitation in holding that proceedings would be said to have been pending only if cognizance had been taken by the Court and steps had been taken by the Court under Chapter XVI of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Since,
there was no cognizance taken, there would be no question of proceedings pending before a criminal Court,
 which would attract the provisions of Section 6(2)(f) of the Passports Act, 1967."
7.
In the case at hand, the Criminal Court has taken cognizance, in fact, C.C.No.334 of 2018 is coming up for trial.

8. Given the facts and circumstances of the case, this Writ Petition is disposed of at the admission stage, with the consent of learned counsel on either side, giving liberty to the petitioner to approach I Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Visakhapatnam by making proper application to seek appropriate orders.
